correctness.rationale: For \(n<b^{K-r}\), a \(K\)-digit padded representation starts with at least \(r\) zeros, so every occurrence of a pattern containing a nonzero digit lies within it. Complementing \(K\) digits maps integer \(n\) to \(b^K-1-n\) and bijects interior occurrences. Outside the complemented word, only one boundary-crossing zero-prefix/maximum-digit-suffix occurrence can arise; it is the constant \(\chi(\bar v)\), independent of n. Reversing any length-\(L\) arithmetic progression about \(b^K-1\) at a sufficiently large \(K\) preserves its positive difference and uniformly translates colors, so sets of monochromatic lengths include each other after exchanging patterns. Finite or infinite suprema therefore agree. Standalone diagnostic code from the package passed 158464 integer identities and 142800 finite progression-transfer cases; proof does not rely on finite extrapolation.

The present finite-trace transport is stronger, includes arbitrary bases and moduli, and is not implied by the inspected group-structured automatic-sequence progression estimates or the named-sequence results. No inspected published statement provides the all-pattern reflection identity or its fixed-difference consequence. An unindexed equivalent digital-reflection argument is a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: Sobolewski (arXiv:2204.05287, §6 Problem 4) explicitly asks to characterize d for complementary-pattern equality and conjectures the all-difference answer for binary non-extreme patterns, supported only by small experiments. This theorem proves that complete conjectured class across all pattern lengths and differences, and extends it in a single structural statement to any base and modulus, answering a concrete aspect of Problem 10. A finite-trace reversal law provides the motivated mechanism and strengthens mere numerical equality; this is a natural mathematical gap, not an arbitrary sample or known-table recomputation.
